short: A tribute empire built in under a century and destroyed in two years.
full:
In 1428 Tenochtitlan, Texcoco and Tlacopan combined against their Tepanec overlords and destroyed Azcapotzalco. The Triple Alliance that followed is what is usually meant by the Aztec Empire. It ruled indirectly, leaving local dynasties in place and taking tribute in cotton, cacao, feathers and captives, recorded in pictorial registers. Tenochtitlan itself stood on an island in Lake Texcoco, reached by causeways and fed by chinampa plots, and held perhaps 200,000 people, more than any city in Spain.

Hernan Cortes landed in 1519 with about 500 men and found allies among subject peoples, above all the never-conquered Tlaxcalans. Moctezuma II died in Spanish custody in 1520; smallpox arrived the same year, killed his successor Cuitlahuac and a large share of the population. Tenochtitlan fell after a siege on 13 August 1521. Mexico City was built directly on the ruins, its cathedral raised from the stones of the demolished temple precinct.
